ei.subject: 수능특강

fullPassage: The emotional tenor of our conversations may be particularly important in a child's early years. Indeed, family dialogues from decades past may still be influencing your mental health today. To understand why, we need a quick primer on the development of our autobiographical memories. In the first few years of life, most children can remember only the slimmest pieces of their experiences — the feel of sand on the beach and the prick of a needle in a doctor's surgery. These may get more detailed as the child learns more and more vocabulary, but they are largely disconnected from each other; they remain isolated sketches of single events. It is only after years of development that the child can slot their recollections into a narrative that has a coherent structure. By the end of adolescence, that narrative may adopt the form of a novel. The teen will start to recognise key events as turning points, with new 'chapters' that represent new eras. The psychologist Dan McAdams at Northwestern University in Illinois describes this as the transition from 'actor' to 'author'.

det.korean: ③ scatter → slot: '기억을 서사에 흩뿌리다(scatter)'는 문맥과 맞지 않음. slot(끼워 넣다, 배치하다)이 올바름. 발달 후 기억을 일관된 서사에 '배치할 수 있다'는 맥락. ← 정답

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 발달을 거친 후 아이는 기억을 __________ 구조를 가진 서사에 배치할 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① coherent(일관된): 'a narrative that has a coherent structure'에서 발달 후 기억이 일관된 구조의 서사로 조직된다는 원문과 일치 ← 정답

❌ ③ emotional(감정적인): 글의 도입부에서 emotional tenor를 언급하지만, 여기서는 서사의 구조적 특성을 말하는 맥락

det.korean: 십대는 핵심 사건들을 __________으로 인식하기 시작한다.

det.tip: turning point(전환점)는 '방향이 바뀌는 지점'으로, 새로운 장(chapter)과 시대(era)가 시작되는 것과 자연스럽게 연결됩니다.
